mayuri-veena.name: Mayuri Veena / Taus
mayuri-veena.resonator_material: seasoned jackfruit or tun wood with calf parchment chest
mayuri-veena.number_of_strings: 4 main bowed strings + 28 to 30 sympathetic tarab resonance strings
mayuri-veena.bridge_type: high arched camel-bone or wood bowing bridge
distinctive_features: sculpted peacock head neck and colorful painted wooden tail feathers
parchment covered soundbox chest
dense row of 28 to 30 side wooden sympathetic pegs
high arched bowing bridge resting on parchment membrane
metal frets tied along the fingerboard
mayuri-veena.playing_posture: seated on floor held vertically or diagonally across lap played with a heavy horsehair bow

rudra-veena.name: Rudra Veena (Dhrupad Been)
rudra-veena.resonator_shape: twin gourd (two massive round spherical tumbas)
rudra-veena.resonator_material: dried seasoned round pumpkin bottle gourds (Lagenaria siceraria) with teak/bamboo dandi
rudra-veena.number_of_strings: 4 main melody strings + 3 side chikari rhythm drone strings
rudra-veena.bridge_type: wide flat bone or horn jivari buzzing bridge
distinctive_features: two massive spherical gourds mounted beneath the tubular neck
22 to 24 high raised brass frets (parda) fixed onto tubular dandi with beeswax
wide flat jivari bridge producing continuous microtonal buzzing overtones
carved makara or bird finial at the head of the dandi
rudra-veena.playing_posture: seated cross-legged in vajrasana/padmasana held diagonally with upper gourd resting on left shoulder and lower gourd on right thigh

yazh.name: Yazh (Ancient Tamil Open Harp)
yazh.resonator_material: hollow seasoned jackfruit wood covered with thin calf parchment skin
yazh.neck_length_category: curved open bow arm (thandu) without neck or frets
yazh.number_of_strings: 7 to 21 open silk or gut strings
yazh.bridge_type: integral wooden string anchoring bar along parchment
distinctive_features: open arched bow harp frame without a central fingerboard
carved makara (mythical sea creature) or peacock head terminal
parchment soundboard covering boat-shaped cavity
leather tuning rings (thimar) along the curved bow arm
yazh.playing_posture: held diagonally or horizontally against torso plucked delicately with bare fingers without plectrum

shankha.name: Shankha (Sacred Ritual Conch)
shankha.resonator_material: natural white calcium carbonate marine sea shell (Turbinella pyrum)
distinctive_features: smooth porcelain-like white spiraled calcareous shell body
perforated apex embouchure mouthpiece
engraved silver or brass ritual filigree mounts and deity motifs
expanding spiral aperture
shankha.playing_posture: held with both hands to mouth blown with high air pressure and vibrating lip embouchure

jal-tarang.name: Jal Tarang (Porcelain Water Chime)
jal-tarang.resonator_shape: semicircular crescent array of graduated circular cups
jal-tarang.resonator_material: fine china porcelain or bronze ceramic bowls with water
distinctive_features: crescent arc of 14 to 22 graduated porcelain water bowls
varying water levels forming microtonal tuning boundaries
pair of slender flexible bamboo striking sticks (tilli)
played seated in the center of the bowl semicircle
jal-tarang.playing_posture: seated on floor in the center of crescent bowl arrangement striking bowl rims with two wooden or bamboo sticks

nagfani.name: Nagfani (Serpentine Brass Horn)
nagfani.resonator_shape: serpentine S-shaped curved tubing with expanded serpent hood bell
nagfani.resonator_material: sheet brass or cast bronze with chased scale engravings
distinctive_features: coiled S-shaped winding tubular body
dramatically expanded bell sculpted like an open cobra hood (phan)
engraved reptile scales and mythological guardian imagery
cupped brass embouchure mouthpiece
nagfani.playing_posture: held vertically in one or both hands with serpent hood flared upwards blown vigorously during temple and martial fanfares

pakhawaj.name: Pakhawaj (Dhrupad Barrel Drum)
pakhawaj.resonator_material: seasoned dense sheesham, jackfruit, or red sandalwood with animal parchment heads
distinctive_features: horizontal asymmetrical barrel body narrower on treble right side and wider on bass left
black circular iron-oxide syahi harmonic loading patch on right dayan face
freshly applied wheat flour and water dough on left bayan face for deep sub-bass pitch bends
cylindrical wooden tuning blocks (gatta) inserted under braided buffalo hide tension straps
pakhawaj.playing_posture: rested horizontally on floor or lap played with open palms and flat-finger slaps (thap) on both drumheads

algoza.name: Algoza (Twin Fipple Flute)
algoza.resonator_material: sheesham wood, wild bamboo, or seasoned brass-banded reed
distinctive_features: two matched parallel wooden flutes held together in mouth
beak-shaped fipple mouthpieces on both pipes
one pipe for continuous drone notes and one for melody
six finger holes per tube played simultaneously with continuous circular breathing
algoza.playing_posture: held vertically outwards with both mouthpieces in mouth, played with continuous circular breathing

ravanahatha.name: Ravanahatha (Desert Spike Fiddle)
ravanahatha.resonator_shape: hemispherical half coconut cup with spike shaft
ravanahatha.resonator_material: seasoned half coconut shell covered with goat hide parchment and long bamboo pole
ravanahatha.number_of_strings: 2 main melody strings (gut and steel) + 12 to 14 side sympathetic metal strings
ravanahatha.bridge_type: carved wood/bone bridge standing on membrane
distinctive_features: halved coconut shell resonator covered with skin
long bamboo dandi shaft passing through soundbox as a spike
prominent curved horsehair bow adorned with dangling brass ghungroo jingle bells
wooden friction tuning pegs along the bamboo neck
ravanahatha.playing_posture: held against left chest and shoulder, bowed with curved bell-bow in rhythmic sweeping strokes

pena.name: Pena (Meitei Ritual Lute)
pena.resonator_material: coconut shell covered with monitor lizard or calfskin parchment and slender bamboo stem (nakong)
distinctive_features: single continuous horsehair chord
carved iron or brass curved bow called Pena Cheijing with tiny chiming metal bells (zor)
bamboo shaft inserted into coconut cup with engraved geometric tribal patterns
pena.playing_posture: held across torso with left hand stopping string with fingernails, bowed with curved Pena Cheijing

morchang.name: Morchang / Morsing (Classical Jaw Harp)
morchang.resonator_shape: horseshoe or lyre-shaped rigid frame with slender central tongue
morchang.resonator_material: forged wrought iron or brass frame with tempered steel reed tongue
distinctive_features: horseshoe-shaped forged metal frame with two parallel prongs
flexible central vibrating steel tongue (zaban) with hooked trigger tip
player's oral cavity acts as variable acoustic resonator
compact handheld size (10 to 15 cm)
morchang.playing_posture: frame pressed firmly against front teeth, tongue plucked with right index finger while changing mouth shape for harmonic filtering

kinnera.name: Kinnera (Three-Gourd Tribal Zither)
kinnera.resonator_shape: triple gourd (three dried spherical gourds in a row)
kinnera.resonator_material: three dried pumpkin gourds tied beneath a bamboo or hollow wood beam
kinnera.neck_length_category: long straight wooden beam with frets
distinctive_features: three spherical gourds attached along the bottom of the beam
frets carved out of animal bone (pangolin or bull bone) fixed with herbal wax
carved bird or fish finial at top of beam
distinctive tribal ballad instrument of Chenchu and Dakkali communities
kinnera.playing_posture: held horizontally or diagonally across the lap/chest, plucked while narrating historical epics

pinaka-veena.name: Pinaka Veena (Shaivite Bow Zither)
pinaka-veena.resonator_shape: curved arch bow-frame with gourd resonator
pinaka-veena.resonator_material: seasoned bamboo bow shaft with dried gourd and silk/gut chord
distinctive_features: constructed like Lord Shiva's divine Pinaka bow
played using a horsehair or resin-coated wooden friction stick
single hollow resonator at the base
ancient Vedic and Shaivite sacred iconography
pinaka-veena.playing_posture: held diagonally resting lower bow end on the floor, rubbed and bowed along the string
